policy.rule: Every new Firestore collection that stores queue, job, lease, dispatch, retry, progress or recovery state must declare a read budget here in the same pull request that introduces it (M8, firestore-reads-program).
policy.surfaces: Python under backend/ (.collection, .collection_group) and TypeScript/JavaScript under web/ (db.collection, db.collectionGroup, collection(db, ...), doc(db, ...)).
policy.kill_switch: FIRESTORE_COLLECTION_BUDGET_GUARD_ENABLED=0 disables the guard for an approved rollback and requires FIRESTORE_COLLECTION_BUDGET_GUARD_DISABLE_REASON.
policy.note: The guard is diff-scoped: a collection or computed site that already exists at the merge base is grandfathered, so these lists start empty and grow one reviewed entry per new work-state collection. A grandfathered computed site whose literal namespace tuple grows keeps its site::expression key, so the guard also compares the enumerable collection family between revisions and requires a budget or exemption for each new member. Offline fixtures in .github/scripts/test_check_firestore_collection_budget.py prove both directions for literal and computed names on both surfaces, for computed-family expansion, and for Python collection_group_id.

entry_fields.collection: Firestore collection id, snake_case or camelCase
entry_fields.owner: lane that owns the collection and its budget
entry_fields.unit: unit of work the per-unit budget divides by (job, batch unit, active user-day, ...)
entry_fields.reads_per_unit_budget: positive integer, reads per unit of work
entry_fields.reads_per_day_budget: positive integer, reads per day at the expected volume
entry_fields.basis: measured (settled billing or a caller counter) or planning-bound (an estimate, never booked as a saving)
entry_fields.source: where the number came from: query, dashboard, or document
entry_fields.reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD date the budget was reviewed

dynamic_entry_fields.site: repository-relative path of the file that computes the name
dynamic_entry_fields.expression: the computed argument exactly as the scanner prints it (for example f'new_{stage}_jobs')
dynamic_entry_fields.collection_pattern: the collection family the expression can produce (for example new_*_jobs)
dynamic_entry_fields.owner: lane that owns the family and its budget
dynamic_entry_fields.unit: unit of work the per-unit budget divides by
dynamic_entry_fields.reads_per_unit_budget: positive integer, reads per unit of work for the whole family
dynamic_entry_fields.reads_per_day_budget: positive integer, reads per day for the whole family
dynamic_entry_fields.reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD date the budget was reviewed

budgets.unit: conversation delete accepted behind a busy account gate
budgets.source: Read path in database/conversation_batch_purge_jobs.py + conversation_tombstones.accept_deletion: accept txn 3, due scans ~3, claim/begin/finish 3, tombstone 1, ~2 busy retries x 4; reconciler empty polls 1,440/day. Volume: prod Cloud Run request logs 2026-11-12 17:30 UTC onward, 1,021 phone cascade deletes in ~18 h (~1,400/day) as an all-accepted upper bound.

dynamic.unit: one maintenance-leader sample at up to 100,000 fresh results per window per environment
dynamic.source: SCA-2012: two count aggregations per 60s per prod/dev leader; each costs max(1, ceil(index entries/1000)); 100,000 total and <=100,000 pending => 200/sample, 288,000/day/environment. Not a throughput cap; revisit budget if cohorts exceed this planning envelope. Normally empty/small windows cost 2/sample. Existing lease check adds <=1 metadata read per maintenance call outside this count budget.

dynamic.unit: one maintenance-leader sample of the admitted-unit cohort
dynamic.source: One bounded metadata page per 300s per prod/dev leader, ordered by enqueued_at and capped at PAGE_LIMIT=5000 document reads: 5,000 x 288 = 1,440,000/day/environment. Normal cohort is ~2,800 units at the 2026-11 peak (~800k/day); a saturated page is reported by omi_batch_pipeline_delivered_share_truncated. Metadata only: no transcript, audio, user id or email. Revisit if admission volume triples or the cohort grows.

dynamic.unit: one retained result read per unstamped job in a backfill window
dynamic.source: Operator-run only, never scheduled. The same bounded job page is read per 15-minute window; rows without the acknowledge stamp get one get_all read each, so a full-day backfill is one result read per admitted unit (~400k at the 2026-11 peak). No transcript field is selected or printed; only projection_state, projection.persisted_at and projection_parts persisted_at.
